reason: Verified by driving master.html?v=approach&state=loading-slow in chromium at 390x844 and 1440x960: press 'Try again', wait 1.4s for the simulated failure, and three paragraphs are visible simultaneously - .b-sub y=321 'This is taking longer than it should.' (15px, fore-62), .b-note y=352 'The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' (13px, rgba(255,255,255,0.62)), .b-live y=383 'Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' (13px, rgb(255,255,255)). The ten-word clause is verbatim identical, 31px apart, both painted, and the repeat is the louder of the two because .b-live is set at full --fore while .b-note is --fore-62. The finding's claim that this is not a screen-reader-only duplicate is correct: b.css line 984 gives .b-live real type and colour and no clip; only the .b-live.b-vh regions at render-b.js 1223 and 1276 are hidden, and shell.css:253 confirms .b-vh is the visually-hidden class. render-b.js:1708 sets the doubled string, and the handler restores note.style.display = '' at the same moment, so the two are deliberately on screen together. Not covered by lessons.md, not asserted by either gate, and not a re-raise of anything refuted in round 7. At a Linear/Stripe bar, saying the same ten words twice inside four lines on the one screen where a guest meets failure is a real copy defect. BUT the proposed fix as written is wrong and must not be taken literally: interaction-check.mjs:2530-2531 asserts 'a second failure still says nothing is lost' via /link still works/i against .b-live.textContent, so trimming the announcement to 'Still not arriving.' fails a passing behaviour gate - and it fails it for a reason. Focus stays on the retry button (the gate proves this too), so the polite live region is the only thing a screen-reader user hears; the static note above is not re-announced by a display flip, and stripping the reassurance from the announcement would leave that user told of failure and nothing about safety. The defect is confirmed; the fix is replaced by the sharpened one below, which removes the visible echo without touching a single word of what is spoken.
sharpenedFix: Do not shorten the announcement. Instead, in the retry click handler in render-b.js (~1707), stop restoring the now-superseded static note: drop the note.style.display = "" line in the failure branch so the reassurance is stated once, by the live region, in the voice that is actually new. The screen after a failed retry then reads 'This is taking longer than it should.' / 'Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' - two lines, no verbatim repeat, the reassurance carried at full ink where it now belongs. Verified in-page by simulation: both gate assertions still pass (/still not arriving/ and /link still works/ against .b-live), and the field settles at 462px against 470px at rest, so the 'Try again' button moves 8px up rather than the 19px down it moves today - strictly less displacement under the press point than the current behaviour. If the note must stay put for geometry, the alternative is to keep .b-note visible and blank the shared clause from the live string while adding a sibling p.b-live.b-vh that carries the full sentence for announcement only - but that costs a second region and a double announcement risk, so prefer the one-line deletion.
